slides.title: Guided Practice: Step-by-Step Model Answers

interactiveCells.question: Step 1: Oxygen Analysis
interactiveCells.expectedAnswer:
Data: Early = 0%, Modern = 21%.
Mechanism: The evolution of algae and green plants introduced photosynthesis, which outputs O2 as a product.

interactiveCells.question: Step 2: Carbon Dioxide Analysis
interactiveCells.expectedAnswer:
Data: Early = ~95%, Modern = 0.04%.
Mechanism 1: Earth cooled, water vapour condensed into oceans; CO2 dissolved into oceans to form carbonate precipitates & sedimentary rocks.
Mechanism 2: Photosynthetic life absorbed remaining CO2 to produce glucose.

interactiveCells.question: Step 3: Nitrogen Analysis
interactiveCells.expectedAnswer:
Data: Early = ~1% (Trace), Modern = 78%.
Mechanism: Nitrogen is highly unreactive. Once released by volcanoes, it slowly built up over billions of years without being consumed by chemical reactions.

slides.text:
Guided Practice: Data Analysis Workshop - Model Answers
Data Investigation: Compare the early atmosphere to the modern atmosphere.
Chart A (Early): 95% CO2, 4% Water Vapour, 1% Trace
Chart B (Modern): 78% N2, 21% O2, 1% Other

Step-by-Step Model Answer:
Step 1: Oxygen Analysis: Early = 0%, Modern = 21%. Photosynthesis produced O2.
Step 2: Carbon Dioxide Analysis: Early = 95%, Modern = 0.04%. Dissolved in oceans / rocks and used in photosynthesis.
Step 3: Nitrogen Analysis: Early = ~1%, Modern = 78%. Nitrogen is unreactive and accumulated.
